name: Blast-resistant buildings
principle: Occupied buildings inside blast overpressure range are engineered to protect people, not just stand up: energy-absorbing steel or reinforced concrete construction, controlled response (ductile, repairable deformation rather than brittle failure), protected openings, and anchored doors and HVAC. Design starts from a siting study and quantified overpressure/impulse from dispersion and explosion modelling (API RP 752/753 onshore; temporary refuge criteria offshore), then verifies member response against that loading.

process_steps.name: Siting study quantifies overpressure and impulse at each occupied building
Building designed for the design blast with acceptable response limits
Module or building fabricated and certified
Occupancy controls keep people outside the blast zone where possible

limitations: protection is only as current as the siting study; process changes move the blast contour
windows, doors and penetrations are the weak points and drive certification
advantages: converts an occupied-building risk into a quantified, testable design case
modular blast buildings can be relocated as the plant evolves
